captions.text: 1980: Mafeking is incorporated after a local referendum ('Mafeking, just outside the borders at independence, was incorporated after a local referendum.
25 February 1980: a military coup overthrows Arron's government, led by Dési Bouterse; same state, same land.
1980: Zimbabwe becomes independent under Mugabe.
1980, 12 April: Master Sergeant Samuel Doe's coup overthrows and kills President Tolbert.
1980: the New Hebrides become the independent Republic of Vanuatu.
1980: the New Hebrides become the Republic of Vanuatu.
1980: Espiritu Santo is held by secessionists as Vanuatu becomes independent.
1980: the Santo secession ends.
22 September 1980: Iraq invades Iran along 'a 644 km front'.
1980: Iraq invades Iran.
1980: the Shatt al-Arab becomes the fighting line.
16 December 1980: the Libyan-backed attack takes N'Djamena.
December 1980: Anguilla's separation from Saint Kitts and Nevis is made formal.
1981: Belize is independent.
1981: Operation Protea, South Africa occupies Cunene.
21 September 1981: Belize becomes independent of the United Kingdom.
21 September 1981: Belize becomes independent.
1 November 1981: full independence.
16 November 1981: Libyan forces leave Chad proper.
16 November 1981: the Libyan occupation of the Chadian capital ends with the withdrawal of all Libyan forces from Chad proper.
November 1981: Libyan forces leave Chad proper.
1981: Ciskei is declared independent on 4 December.
14 December 1981: the Golan Heights Law.
14 December 1981: Israel annexes the Golan Heights.
14 December 1981: Israel passes the Golan Heights Law, ending the military occupation of the Golan in favour of annexation.
14 December 1981: Israel annexes the Golan.
1982: Israel completes its withdrawal from the Sinai.
1982: Israel keeps Taba.
1982: Iraq takes its share of the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone.
1982: the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone is partitioned.
1982: Israel invades Lebanon.
1982: the Sinai is Egypt's again.
2 April 1982: Argentina invades and occupies the Falkland Islands.
2 April 1982: Argentina invades the Falklands.
1982: the capital moves from Colombo to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
14 June 1982: the Argentine garrison surrenders at Stanley.
1982: Democratic Kampuchea, the KPNLF and FUNCINPEC form the Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea on 22 June.
14 June 1982: the Argentine garrison surrenders.
June 1982: Iran retakes its land.
1982: Iran retakes Khuzestan.
6 June 1982: Israel invades Lebanon again.
June 1982: Israeli forces reach the Beirut area.
14 June 1982: the siege of Beirut begins.
29 September 1982: Israel leaves west Beirut.
1982: the Kurdish rebellion ends.
1983: 'Colony' becomes 'dependent territory'.
1983: Yamoussoukro becomes the capital.
1983: the SPLA rises in the south.
June 1983: Libya returns to northern Chad.
June 1983: Libya returns to the north.
1983: the second civil war begins in the south.
June 1983: the Bor and Pibor garrisons mutiny and the SPLA is founded.
1983: the war for the south begins (infobox 5 June 1983).
23 July 1983: Iran takes the Iraqi town of Haj Omran.
23 July 1983: Iran takes the Iraqi town of Haj Omran.
3 September 1983: Israel withdraws south of the Awali.
19 September 1983: the UK's responsibility for external affairs and defence ends with full independence.

19 September 1983: Saint Kitts and Nevis becomes fully independent as the Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis ('Today, the Constitution refers to the state as both Saint Kitts and Nevis and Saint Christopher and Nevis'); same state, same land.
25 October 1983: the United States and Caribbean forces invade and occupy Grenada.
1983: the north declares itself the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus on 15 November.
December 1983: US troops withdraw.

1984: Brunei is independent.
1984: back to the Republic of Cameroon.
1 January 1984: independence.
February 1984: Iran takes Majnoon Island.
1984: Iran takes Majnoon Island.
13 April 1984: India occupies the Siachen Glacier region.
13 April 1984: the Siachen conflict begins.
4 August 1984: Upper Volta becomes Burkina Faso.
1985: the Mong Tai Army is founded in the Shan hills.
1985: 'Civilians returned to power in 1985 when José Sarney assumed the presidency.'
1985: the Falkland Islands Dependency is dissolved.
1985: the insurgency in the Shan hills; Homein 'hosted several Shan insurgent groups' from 1985 (Homein page).
1985: Israel pulls back from most of Lebanon.
1985: the South Lebanon Security Belt.
1985: the Republic of Sudan is restored on 6 April.
June 1985: Israel pulls back to a security zone.

June 1985: 'the IDF unilaterally withdrew to a security zone in southern Lebanon' with 'its principal Lebanese ally, the South Lebanon Army', 'completing its troop withdrawal to the security zone on 5 June'; the page names the IDF's final withdrawal in 2000.
25 December 1985: Mali and Burkina Faso fight over the Agacher Strip.
25 December 1985: Mali and Burkina Faso fight over the Agacher Strip.

1986: the Jamahiriya takes its final name.
1 January 1986: Aruba leaves the Netherlands Antilles and becomes a separate country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands ('status aparte').
1 January 1986: Aruba 'seceded' from the Netherlands Antilles; 'In 1986, Aruba became a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands'.
1986 (1 January): Aruba becomes a separate country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, 'status aparte' after a 1977 consultative referendum.
1986: Iran crosses the Shatt al-Arab and takes al-Faw.
April 1986: Qatar acts on Fasht al-Dibal.
April 1986: Qatar acts on Fasht al-Dibal.
1986: the Marshall Islands leave the trust territory: infobox 'Compact of Free Association: October 21, 1986'; 'The islands signed a Compact of Free Association with the United States in 1986.'
1986: the Marshall Islands leave the trust territory: 'On October 21, 1986, the US ended its administration of the Marshall Islands District' (Compact of Free Association effective 21 October 1986).

1986: the Northern Mariana Islands constitution becomes fully effective under the Covenant: 'on November 4, 1986, the Northern Mariana Islands constitution became fully effective under the Covenant' (another passage: implementation 'was completed on November 3, 1986').
1986: the Federated States of Micronesia becomes a sovereign state in free association with the United States.

1986: Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae and Pohnpei leave the trust territory on 3 November 1986: 'Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and the Mariana Islands districts of the TTPI soon followed on November 3, 1986' (COFA effective 3 November 1986 for the Federated States of Micronesia).

1986: the Mariana Islands district leaves on 3 November 1986 to become the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (constitution 'partially effective January 1, 1978, and fully effective November 4, 1986').
22 December 1986: the ICJ ends the Agacher dispute.
22 December 1986: the western part of the Agacher Strip goes to Mali.
22 December 1986: the ICJ ends the Agacher dispute.
22 December 1986: Mali receives the western part of the Agacher Strip.

22 December 1986: the ICJ divided the Agacher Strip: 'Mali received the more-densely populated western portion and Burkina Faso the eastern section centered on the Beli', a strip the page puts at about 160 km long, with no area or coordinates.
1987: the Derg dissolves itself and founds the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia.
1987: the army is 'officially renamed to the MTA'; its declared goal was 'ultimately independence for Shan State'.
8 January 1987: Operation Karbala-5 (the Siege of Basra) opens and Iran takes ground east of Basra.
14 April 1987: Operation Karbala-10 carries Iran and the PUK Peshmerga into Iraqi Kurdistan.
11 September 1987: an OAU-brokered ceasefire ends the Toyota War.
11 September 1987: the OAU ceasefire ends the Toyota War.
1987: after two military coups Fiji is declared a republic.
1987: the Democratic Republic becomes the Republic of Afghanistan.
December 1987: Thailand and Laos fight over Ban Romklao.

19 February 1988: the border war ends.
March 1988: the EPLF takes Afabet.
1988: Iraq retakes al-Faw.
25 May 1988: Iraq clears Iranian forces from the front east of Basra.
25 June 1988: Iraq retakes Majnoon Island.
July 1988: Iraq occupies Iranian land at Dehloran and Qasr-e Shirin (recorded with the roles reversed: the land is Iran's, the occupier is Iraq).

By 12 July 1988: Iraq has cleared its territory of Iranian forces, Haj Omran among it. The infobox has 'Complete elimination of Iranian forces in Iraq (liberating 4,400sq.km)' and 'Iraqi forces regain control over all Iraqi territory previously held by Iranian forces', and the text has Iraq 'in control of virtually all of the Iranian positions on its territory' within hours of 12 July; the page do

By 12 July 1988: the Karbala-10 strip is bridged to the same sweep (confidence 1). No page opened names the ground or says when Iran left it; the Tawakalna page's infobox says Iraq regained 'all Iraqi territory previously held by Iranian forces', and Cliopatria's 1990 shape has none of the 1987 northern cells.
31 July 1988: Jordan gives up the West Bank.
31 July 1988: the West Bank claim passes to the PLO.
31 July 1988: Jordan gives up the West Bank.
31 July 1988: the West Bank is now claimed by the PLO ('Jordan renounced its claims to the West Bank for the PLO').
20 August 1988: the cease-fire ends the Iran-Iraq War and Haj Omran returns to the pre-war line.
20 August 1988: the cease-fire ends the Iran-Iraq War and Majnoon Island returns to the pre-war line ('Status quo ante bellum'; 'The war did not create any permanent border changes').
1988: the ceasefire ends the fighting on the frontier.
August 1988: Iraq withdraws from the Iranian towns after the ceasefire.
1988: South Africa leaves Angola.
5 October 1988: the current constitution is 'promulgated on 5 October 1988' and the last three territories become states ('Amapá and Roraima (which gained statehood)').
1989: Taba is returned to Egypt.
1989 (bridge): the SPLA holds the south outside the government's towns.
1989 (bridge): the SPLA holds the south outside the government's towns.
1989: the Soviet army leaves Afghanistan.
15 February 1989: the last Soviet troops leave.
February 1989: the seven Sunni parties form the Afghan Interim Government.
February 1989: the government in exile sits at Peshawar, Pakistan (infobox headquarters) after 'the groups attempted to form a coalition government in exile from Peshawar'.
1989: the MNDAA is formed on 12 March by Pheung Kya-shin, the head of the CPB's Kokang branch, 'the first one to sign a ceasefire agreement with the Burmese government'.
1989: the Kokang defect.
1989: the Wa State begins on 17 April.
1989: the Wa troops at Panghsang break away.
1989: the CPB collapses at Panghsang on 16-17 April; the breakaway armies sign ceasefires (UWSA on 18 May 1989 per the Wa State text, 9 May per its infobox).

1989: the Communist Party of Burma's armed state ends when 'a group of mutineers stormed the party headquarters in Panghsang' on 16 April 1989; its north-east passes to the Wa State, the Kokang MNDAA and the Mong La NDAA.
1989: the PRK becomes the State of Cambodia.
1989: Burma becomes the Union of Myanmar.
September 1989: the Vietnamese army leaves.
September 1989: Vietnam withdraws from Cambodia.
1989: the Third Republic is established.
1989: the Khmer Rouge take Pailin.
1989: the People's Republic ends on 23 October, the 33rd anniversary of the revolution.
24 October 1989: the Khmer Rouge take Pailin after the Vietnamese withdrawal.
1989-12: Romania, no longer socialist, takes its name after the fall of Ceausescu.
1989: the People's Republic ends and the Third Polish Republic begins.
1989: Ceaușescu falls and the Socialist Republic ends.
